notice: Creator-first reference notes and original editorial heuristics. Apply mechanisms, never copy scripts or impersonate creators. These notes guide prompting, not model-weight training or guaranteed virality.

cards.title: Made to Stick
cards.author: Chip Heath and Dan Heath
cards.principle: One memorable idea benefits from concrete details, credible support and a story with a meaningful stake.
cards.application: Build the script around one observable change; replace abstract benefit lists with a specific scene.
cards.caution: Memorability is not evidence that a product claim is true.

cards.title: Contagious
cards.author: Jonah Berger
cards.principle: People can share useful information, identity signals and stories connected to familiar situations.
cards.application: Give the intended viewer a practical takeaway they could pass to someone in the same situation.
cards.caution: A sharing framework is not a prediction of views or shares.

cards.title: Everybody Writes
cards.author: Ann Handley
cards.principle: Useful marketing content takes deliberate drafting, revision and attention to the reader.
cards.application: Start with the viewer's question, write a plain-language answer, then cut anything that does not help that viewer.
cards.caution: This is an original editorial application, not a reproduction of the book or an effectiveness estimate.

cards.title: Concise, scannable and objective writing
cards.author: Nielsen Norman Group
cards.principle: Web-reading usability improved with concise, scannable and objective copy in the reported study.
cards.application: Use direct spoken sentences, familiar words and one idea at a time. Remove inflated adjectives and repeated claims.
cards.caution: Web-page usability results are not measured short-video retention effects.

cards.title: YouTube thumbnail test and compare
cards.author: YouTube Help
cards.principle: Controlled comparisons and watch-time outcomes can reveal differences that click counts alone miss.
cards.application: Propose two hook variants with the same body and CTA. Record exposure, retention and the primary outcome before declaring a winner.
cards.caution: Thumbnail experiments do not prove a script hook will work; sequential organic posts are confounded.

cards.title: What Makes Online Content Viral?
cards.author: Jonah Berger and Katherine L. Milkman, Journal of Marketing Research (2012)
cards.principle: This research examined sharing of news articles and tested links between emotional activation and transmission.
cards.application: Consider a truthful moment of surprise or useful discovery worth passing on, then test it with the intended audience.
cards.caution: News sharing and laboratory tasks do not establish short-video conversion or retention effects. Do not manufacture fear or outrage.

cards.title: TikTok Creative Codes
cards.author: TikTok for Business
cards.principle: The platform's advertising guidance uses an opening hook, a body that carries the message and a closing action.
cards.application: Build a concise creator-led story with an immediate audience stake, progression and a delivered payoff; adapt advertiser guidance to the selected content mode.
cards.caution: Platform advertising guidance is not an independent causal study or a promise of organic reach.

cards.title: Promise and payoff checklist
cards.author: Studio editorial practice
cards.principle: A hook makes a specific promise; the body must deliver it without misleading the viewer.
cards.application: Write the opening promise and the exact verbal payoff. Remove the hook if its payoff cannot be supplied.
cards.caution: This checklist is an editorial hypothesis, not a published experiment.

cards.title: Shootable story beats
cards.author: Studio editorial practice
cards.principle: Each scene needs a purpose, an observable action and enough time to perform it.
cards.application: Keep the idea simple enough for one creator to express naturally. Write dialogue only, with brief inline cues only when the requested duration requires them.
cards.caution: A shot plan does not establish the quality of actual voice or visuals.

cards.title: Hook experiment protocol
cards.author: Studio editorial practice
cards.principle: Choose the hypothesis and primary metric before collecting results; avoid changing multiple creative variables together.
cards.application: Compare two openings with an otherwise fixed edit. Save platform, audience, dates, impressions, early retention and conversions. Treat small or unmatched samples as inconclusive.
cards.caution: This tool stores user observations; it does not run platform experiments or infer causality from uncontrolled posts.

cards.title: Instagram Best Practices creator hub
cards.author: Meta / Instagram
cards.principle: Instagram's professional dashboard offers creator guidance covering creation, engagement and reach, including account-specific tips.
cards.application: Plan one clear audience moment, then compare it with your own account insights and the in-app guidance. Do not copy an alleged universal algorithm formula.
cards.caution: The announcement describes a guidance hub, not proof that a specific script format will go viral.

cards.title: Instagram Trial Reels experiments
cards.author: Meta / Instagram
cards.principle: Trial Reels let creators try content with non-followers first and inspect engagement before wider sharing.
cards.application: Where available, test a rant against a quieter observation with the same topic. Record views, likes, comments and shares plus differences in timing and audience.
cards.caution: Trial Reels are not randomized script experiments. Feature availability and results vary; do not infer causality from unmatched posts.

cards.title: Instagram creative experimentation
cards.author: Meta / Instagram
cards.principle: Instagram's creativity initiative encourages experimentation and describes tools for trying new ideas.
cards.application: Use the creator's own vocabulary, situation and observation. Change one angle per iteration instead of reproducing another creator's script.
cards.caution: Platform encouragement to experiment is not evidence that copying a trend guarantees reach.

cards.title: One person, one phone, one idea
cards.author: Studio editorial practice
cards.principle: A strong observation can carry a simple direct-to-camera video without a cast or elaborate production.
cards.application: Write for one creator: an opening thought, a short progression and a satisfying payoff. Keep the language easy to say aloud.
cards.caution: Production simplicity is a practical writing constraint, not a measured virality advantage.

cards.title: Relatable mini-rant
cards.author: Studio editorial practice
cards.principle: A specific shared frustration gives a solo creator a natural reason to speak with energy.
cards.application: Start mid-thought, name one annoyance, escalate through two recognizable details, then land a punchline or useful point. Keep the product incidental.
cards.caution: Do not manufacture outrage, shame appearance or invent personal product results to intensify a rant.

cards.title: Routine commentary / GRWM
cards.author: Studio editorial practice
cards.principle: A familiar getting-ready action can provide a simple visual while the creator tells a story or observation.
cards.application: One creator comments on one familiar task with a specific observation. Only describe personal use when the brief supplies that authentic experience.
cards.caution: Do not invent application schedules, combinations or treatment instructions for a haircare or skincare routine.

cards.title: Haircare and skincare: the everyday moment
cards.author: Studio editorial practice
cards.principle: Wash-day planning, bathroom shelves, getting-ready delays and label confusion can be recognizable topics without a sales pitch.
cards.application: Choose one specific annoyance or genuine observation. Let a reaction, self-aware aside or callback deliver the payoff; avoid ingredient recitation and fabricated before/after stories.
cards.caution: Use supplied creator experience for personal stories. A relatable scenario is not clinical evidence or a diagnosis.

cards.title: Low-stakes beauty hot take
cards.author: Studio editorial practice
cards.principle: A clearly framed personal preference can invite conversation without pretending to be a universal scientific rule.
cards.application: Open with a proposed opinion about routine complexity or habits, give one concrete reason, and leave room for viewers to disagree naturally.
cards.caution: Keep opinion separate from ingredient safety, diagnosis, treatment or efficacy claims; those need appropriate factual support.

cards.title: One-question creator reply
cards.author: Studio editorial practice
cards.principle: One focused question can provide a complete solo-video structure with little production overhead.
cards.application: Use a real supplied comment, or label a question as hypothetical. Answer it directly, give one useful example and stop when the question is resolved.
cards.caution: Do not invent follower comments, fake screenshots, endorsements or professional credentials.

cards.title: Two or three small observations
cards.author: Studio editorial practice
cards.principle: A short list works best when its items develop one recognizable topic rather than unrelated tips.
cards.application: Use two or three concrete observations about the same everyday situation. Keep each line brief and finish with the strongest point or callback.
cards.caution: Do not turn the list into unsupported medical advice, a feature dump or a guaranteed growth formula.

cards.title: Emotional recognition before promotion
cards.author: Creator Studio editorial desk
cards.principle: Start with a specific feeling the audience recognizes; move it toward relief, delight, curiosity or a laugh.
cards.application: Choose one small audience tension. Make the opening recognizable, then deliver an emotional turn through a concrete observation.
cards.caution: Do not manufacture shame, anxiety or false personal testimony.

cards.title: The send-this-to-a-friend test
cards.author: Creator Studio editorial desk
cards.principle: Sharing can express identity, a shared frustration, useful knowledge or an inside joke.
cards.application: Name the recognizable situation precisely enough that a viewer knows which friend would understand it. Earn the share through the idea rather than begging for engagement.
cards.caution: Shareability is a hypothesis to test, not a predicted outcome.

cards.title: A product with a role in the story
cards.author: Creator Studio editorial desk
cards.principle: An influencer earns attention through an idea; the product participates in the payoff.
cards.application: Build a rant, discovery, comparison or tiny story worth watching on its own. Connect one verified product fact to that moment. Use one understated, concrete CTA when required.
cards.caution: Never invent usage, results, sensory experience, prices or sponsorship status. Keep paid relationships transparent when supplied.

cards.title: Curiosity with an honest payoff
cards.author: Creator Studio editorial desk
cards.principle: An opening creates a promise which the ending must satisfy.
cards.application: Open on a specific odd detail, reversal or unresolved observation. Add information with each sentence; resolve the exact promise before the CTA.
cards.caution: Avoid empty cliffhangers and bait with no answer.

cards.title: Specificity across creator niches
cards.author: Creator Studio editorial desk
cards.principle: Relatable detail gives a familiar format its own voice.
cards.application: Skincare: routine confusion without medical promises. Fashion: a styling dilemma. Food/drinks: a grounded preference, not invented tasting. FMCG: an everyday annoyance. Arcade: playful competition without invented wins. Pick one situation, not a feature checklist.
cards.caution: All product assertions must come from the brief; comedy does not excuse fabricated proof.

cards.title: Hindi, English and Hinglish that sound spoken
cards.author: Creator Studio editorial desk
cards.principle: A creator speaks in audience idiom rather than translating advertising slogans.
cards.application: Use the requested language and script consistently. Prefer everyday phrasing, contractions, rhythmic pauses and culturally intelligible jokes; preserve only natural code-switches.
cards.caution: Do not caricature an accent or use stereotypes as a shortcut.

cards.title: YouTube Shorts: audience and first seconds
cards.author: YouTube
cards.principle: Choose a recognizable niche idea and establish its appeal in the first few seconds.
cards.application: Use a solo creator observation, useful tip or comic moment, with one clear payoff. Adapt the principle to the brief rather than copying a popular clip.
cards.caution: Official guidance does not establish a guaranteed ranking formula.
